The fund still manages over $10 billion, including a $5 billion stake in Anthropic, whose shares began trading on Nasdaq November 19 at $83 under ticker ANT—though Wall Street skeptics question returning to leverage so soon after the near-collapse.

Talks started before former CEO Jensen Huang's resignation, following Inception's $50 million seed round backed by Nvidia's venture arm, signaling the chip giant's push into AI software amid competition.

data.name: Sarvam AI Launches Token Factory Hosting Foreign Models on Indian GPUs
data.summary: On November 16, Sarvam AI debuted Token Factory, an inference platform on Indian GPU clusters that serves its own 105B model plus open-weight systems from DeepSeek, Moonshot, Zhipu AI, and Google's Gemma through a single OpenAI-compatible API. Critics say it undercuts Sarvam's government-subsidized push for sovereign AI, acting more like a hosting service for foreign tech despite ₹98.68 crore in subsidies and $234 million raised. Supporters highlight benefits like data staying in India, competitive rupee pricing around ₹14 per million input tokens, low latency, and revenue to fund bigger domestic models—all on separate private infrastructure.

Online reactions blend excitement with memes, like one showing stunned bank staff as AI finally acts on months of meeting talks.

data.summary: Jasmine Sun's New York Times piece reveals Anthropic staff's deep commitment to steering AI away from catastrophe, shaped by CEO Dario Amodei's view that their leadership offers the safest path forward.
